Before the European Bell: Earnings Enter the Home Stretch
By Neil Campling
08/10/2026 01:35:41 [BFW]
(Bloomberg) -- Stocks look set for a muted start to the week, as an anticipated deal to formally reopen the Strait of Hormuz remained elusive and oil prices ticked higher. Eyes will be on whether earnings can sustain a run that’s outpacing expectations.
Euro Stoxx 50 futures were steady at 7:25 a.m. CET, while contracts on the FTSE 100 were down 0.4%. 
Asian stocks are mixed, with Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 up 2.0% to lead the region as the Yen weakens through the session. Futures point to modest gains in the US later. Brent crude is slightly higher than when Europe went home Friday, after Yemen’s Houthi militants attacked an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia on Sunday. 
Markets at a Glance: 
 
Source: Bloomberg
Economic growth in the euro zone is set to quicken after showing surprising resilience to the Iran war, according to a Bloomberg survey of analysts. The 21-nation bloc is forecast to expand 0.8% in 2026, up from a 0.5% estimate in July. 
With about 80% of Stoxx 600 companies having reported and Q2 EPS growth near 20%, the focus shifts to whether the final stretch can sustain the recent run of beats and guidance upgrades. 
Adyen, E.ON and Aviva are among corporates set to announce numbers this week. A relatively quiet lineup on the macro agenda includes UK and Swiss second quarter GDP data. Bloomberg Strategist Ruhell Amin poses three questions for the week ahead: Can Europe keep climbing after outrunning consensus? Will earnings keep doing the heavy lifting? Does the US-Iran détente hold? 
 
Europe’s stock market is firing on all cylinders and drawing money managers who say this rally will be more durable than just another short-term trade. Whether it’s earnings, economic growth, sentiment surveys or fund flows, market metrics across the board show a major shift is underway in European stocks. 
 
In geopolitics, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu hardened his position and rejected a proposal by US-backed mediators for disarming Hamas. A mutual defense pact between Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan could be expanded to include other regional states including Egypt, Turkey’s foreign minister said. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is embarking on a nationwide tour to promote new policies aimed at reducing the cost of living.
In other assets, highly-indebted companies are increasingly ditching private credit loans for cheaper capital in the bank loan market, a shift underscoring the stark realities of higher-for-longer interest rates. US wheat futures jumped to the highest in more than a week, as disruptions to shipping in the Black Sea raised the prospect of supply shortages from the crucial grain-growing region. 
Hungary’s central bank renewed its support for the government’s efforts to meet conditions for joining the euro area, saying it would benefit the economy. Elsewhere, Italy’s record-low Po River delta, a district accounting for about 41% of Italy’s GDP, is forcing farmers to rethink what they grow. 
In deals, Israel is currently expected to reject the proposed sale of ZIM shipping company to Hapag-Lloyd and FIMI investment fund, Calcalist reports. EasyJet is said to be discussing deepening arrangements with Virgin Atlantic, according to The Sunday Times.

Before the European Bell: Big Bank Beats Offset Oil Rise
By Farah Elbahrawy and Neil Campling
07/29/2026 01:36:38 [BFW]
(Bloomberg) -- European stock futures are trimming early losses as strong earnings beats from banks are helping to offset pressure from higher oil prices and AI spending fears.
Euro Stoxx 50 futures were down 0.3% at 7:25 a.m. CET, while contracts on the FTSE 100 were 0.2% lower. Brent crude surged after the US said it intercepted an Iranian attack on military bases, ending a dayslong pause in fighting.
In Asia, SK Hynix shares tumbled as much as 20% after earmarking at least $31 billion for capital spending this year, adding to concerns that tech companies are overinvesting in AI. It sent the Kospi down as much as 13%.
 
The AI trade has come under even more scrutiny this week as investors question whether massive spending across the ecosystem will pay off. In Europe, perceived AI laggards are outperforming winners by a record margin in July. The focus will turn to spending figures from Meta and Microsoft which report after the US close later.
 
Over 50 companies on the Stoxx Europe 600 are reporting results Wednesday. The banks are a bright spot, as Standard Chartered announced a $1 billion share buyback as it reported second-quarter earnings that beat expectations. 
UBS profit also surpassed estimates and it announced a new $3 billion share buyback program to run until mid-2027. Deutsche Bank’s FIC sales & trading revenue for the second quarter beat the average analyst estimate, and the German bank announced a a new share buyback of €500 million.
Other highlights include Kering, whose ADRs surged after reporting that Gucci sales fell less than expected in the second quarter, suggesting efforts to revive the brand are starting to bear fruit. EssilorLuxottica said revenue from the Ray-Ban owner’s category-leading smartglasses nearly doubled in the second quarter. Meanwhile, Rio Tinto reported first-half underlying profit that beat the average analyst estimate, with strong copper earnings.
HSBC strategist Duncan Toms sees reasons to be optimistic about European equities in the second half. “Top down macro expectations could prove too pessimistic, particularly if higher policy uncertainty and currently hawkish ECB rate pricing unwind,” he writes. “Bottom up, earnings expectations have been more resilient with Q2 expected to be the strongest second quarter in three years.”
 
Out of the MSCI Europe companies that have reported so far this season, 47% have beaten expectations while 31% have missed. 
The attention will turn to the Federal Reserve after the close. It’s expected to hold interest rates steady but market participants are eyeing the possibility of a surprise hike as patience with high inflation wears thin.

(Bloomberg) -- European stock futures were steady ahead of the open as investors navigated a packed day of central bank action, key economic data and the busiest earnings slate of the season.
Euro Stoxx 50 futures were flat at 7:26 a.m. CET, while contracts on the FTSE 100 were down 0.9%. 
The session was volatile in Asia, with the Kospi swinging between gains of as much as 5.5% and a loss of as much as 2.1%. A 250-fold jump in Samsung Electronics’ chip profits was only briefly rewarded as investors increasingly question the business case for the massive investments pouring into AI development and data center construction.
Besides earnings, central banks and inflation will also be top of mind on Thursday as Kevin Warsh’s bare-bones communication style left investors doubting his commitment to curb prices. The Bank of England is set to leave interest rates on hold as it sticks to a wait-and-see approach to navigate the wild swings in oil and gas prices.
The unwind out of US tech picked up steam on Wednesday, with the Nasdaq 100 closing in correction territory as investors wagered that the Fed will face increasing pressure to act. Futures are pointing to a positive start in the US later, with Nasdaq contracts leading the advance.
Microsoft was a bright spot afterhours, rallying as its earnings showed that the company’s investments in AI are starting to pay off. Azure cloud revenue beat estimates, while its capital expenditures were lower than expected. On the flip side, Meta Platforms fell as it gave a disappointing quarterly revenue forecast and reported the lowest free cash flow in years, a sign of ballooning expenses for AI bets.
 
Europe’s outperformance versus the US is picking up this earnings season, with the Stoxx 600 up slightly since it began, while the S&P 500 has fallen 2.7%. European results since Wednesday’s close have been largely positive.
Societe Generale raised its profitability target for the year and announced a €1.5 billion share buyback after second-quarter profit beat analysts’ estimates. Airbus reported a 54% increase in second-quarter earnings as aircraft production improved. L’Oreal sales climbed in the second quarter, boosted by growth in all regions.
BBVA posted second-quarter profit that beat analysts’ estimates and announced a new share buyback program for as much as €2 billion. ArcelorMittal reported stronger than expected second-quarter earnings as the European Union moves to bolster its steel industry. AB InBev posted volume growth that narrowly missed expectations.

En el plano corporativo, los resultados del segundo trimestre en **EEUU** marcan la pauta. **Amazon** se disparó más del +9% en el after-hours tras acelerar sus ingresos de **AWS** por quinto trimestre consecutivo, confirmando que el gasto en IA se está traduciendo en crecimiento tangible. En contraste, **Apple** cayó más del -6% tras advertir que la escasez de componentes lastrará sus previsiones de ventas, lo que presionará a proveedores europeos como **STMicro** e **Infineon**. En Europa, **Axa** reportó un beneficio del primer semestre superior al del año anterior, **Crédit Agricole** superó expectativas con récord en gestión de activos, y **Holcim** elevó sus guías anuales. **Alimentation Couche-Tard** acordó comprar una participación de control en la polaca **Żabka** por unos **$8.7bn**. En el ámbito de fondos, el hedge fund **Situational Awareness**, de **Leopold Aschenbrenner**, ha visto caer sus activos a unos **$10bn** después de que **Citadel**, de **Ken Griffin**, comprara el grueso de sus posiciones bursátiles, en un episodio que subraya la tensión de liquidez en estrategias apalancadas de IA.

La agenda macro y de resultados es densa. En **EEUU**, publican hoy antes de la apertura **ExxonMobil**, **Chevron**, **AbbVie**, **Linde**, **Eaton**, **Colgate-Palmolive**, **T. Rowe Price**, **CBOE**, **Roku** y **Moderna**. En Europa, reportan **AXA**, **Crédit Agricole**, **Amadeus**, **Engie**, **Covestro**, **NatWest**, **IAG**, **Puma**, **Siemens Healthineers**, **OMV** y **Unicaja**, entre otros. En el plano macro, la referencia clave es el **IPC de la Eurozona de julio**, que se publica a las 11:00 CET y se espera en el **+2.9% yoy**, una décima por encima del dato anterior, lo que condicionará las expectativas de cara a la reunión de septiembre del **BCE**. Se conocerán también el **IPC de Francia** (est. +1.8% yoy), la **tasa de desempleo alemana** (est. 6.3%) y la **confianza del consumidor italiano** (est. 92.8). En **UK**, destaca el índice de precios de vivienda **Nationwide** de julio (est. +0.1% mom). En **EEUU**, la atención se centrará en los resultados empresariales citados y en la evolución de los futuros tras el fuerte repunte tecnológico de la sesión previa.
